content: 1. For induced abortion at less than 12 weeks of gestation, the recommended regimen includes a single dose of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally, followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally. A repeat dose of 800 μg of misoprostol may be used if necessary. 2. For induced abortion at 12 weeks of gestation or beyond, the regimen involves a single dose of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally, followed by 400 μg of misoprostol administered vaginally, sublingually, or buccally every 3 hours as needed. 3. For missed abortion at less than 14 weeks of gestation, a single dose of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally is followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered buccally, vaginally, or sublingually. Repeat doses of 800 μg of misoprostol may be used if necessary. 4. For intrauterine fetal demise between 14 and 28 weeks of gestation, a single dose of 200 mg of mifepristone taken orally is followed by 400 μg of misoprostol administered sublingually (preferred) or vaginally every 4–6 hours. The dose of misoprostol should be reduced for gestational ages beyond 24 weeks due to limited data and increased uterine sensitivity to prostaglandins. 5. For incomplete abortion at less than 14 weeks of gestation, the recommended regimen is 600 μg of misoprostol taken orally or 400 μg administered sublingually. 6. For incomplete abortion at 14 weeks of gestation or beyond, 400 μg of misoprostol is administered sublingually, vaginally, or buccally every 3 hours as needed. 7. For induced abortion at less than 12 weeks of gestation using a letrozole-misoprostol regimen, 10 mg of letrozole is taken orally daily for 3 days, followed by 800 μg of misoprostol administered sublingually on the fourth day. 8. Hormonal contraception can be initiated immediately after the first pill of a medical abortion regimen. Intrauterine devices (IUDs) can be inserted after confirming the successful completion of the abortion. 9. The combination regimen of mifepristone and misoprostol is slightly more effective than misoprostol alone. Repeat doses of misoprostol can be considered as needed to achieve the desired outcome. There is no specific recommendation for the maximum number of misoprostol doses, but healthcare providers should use clinical judgment, especially in individuals with a history of uterine incision, as uterine rupture is a rare but serious complication. 10. Uterine size increases by approximately 1 cm per week after 4 weeks of gestation. By 12 weeks, the uterus rises out of the pelvis, and by 20 weeks, it reaches the umbilicus. After 20 weeks, fundal height in centimeters roughly corresponds to the gestational age in weeks. 11. Pregnancy dating can be based on the last menstrual period (LMP) alone or in combination with validated tools. If LMP is uncertain, a clinical examination may be warranted. The least invasive method appropriate to the circumstances should be used. 12. Information is a critical component of medical care and should always be provided to individuals considering abortion. Counseling should be a focused, interactive process conducted in a supportive environment to facilitate open communication. 13. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) should be offered for pain management during medical abortion to those who desire them. 14. Routine follow-up is not necessary after an uncomplicated medical abortion using mifepristone and/or misoprostol. However, individuals should be informed about the availability of additional services if needed or desired.
